# Vendored: TSANet Connect Core API spec

`openapi.yaml` here is a **byte-identical copy** of the transport contract that
`connect-library`'s codegen consumes. It is vendored so CI can build the `sdk`
profile without reaching into a private repository.

## Provenance

| field | value |
|---|---|
| source repo | `tsanetgit/Connect-API-Code` (private) |
| source path | `connect-core-api/src/main/resources/openapi.yaml` |
| ref | `beta` — `develop` breaks codegen (V2 webhook APIs) |
| commit | `0691e1fef3b9983c031ec4dfa92f5417b048bc3a` |
| commit date | 2026-07-15T15:44:57Z |
| vendored | 2026-08-06 |
| sha256 | `0474ae07825683438df06a2c54377c8971496ffbe763a15f3713a34bdfb48f0e` |
| size | 80142 bytes |

**Do not edit this file.** Its whole value is being byte-identical to upstream:
that is what makes drift a one-line hash comparison instead of a diff review.
Provenance lives here in the sidecar for the same reason — a header comment
inside the YAML would break the comparison.

## Why it is vendored rather than checked out

`connect-library` (in the public `shawn-tsanet/connect-sdk-demo`) resolves the
spec through the Maven property `connect.openapi.spec`, defined in that repo's
parent `pom.xml` as a sibling path `../Connect-API-Code/...` and used exactly
once, as `<inputSpec>` in `connect-library/pom.xml`. Satisfying that sibling in
CI previously meant checking out the private `Connect-API-Code`, which needed a
cross-org token (`CONNECT_API_CODE_TOKEN`). That secret was never configured, so
the whole `sdk` job skipped every real step **while reporting success** — the
connector's gateway tests, including the sanitizer drift guard, had never once
executed in CI.

A fine-grained PAT for an org-owned repo needs `tsanetgit` owner approval, and a
deploy key needs admin on `Connect-API-Code`; neither is self-service here. One
80 KB file was the entire dependency, so vendoring removes the credential from
the build instead of provisioning one.

## Refreshing

```bash
gh api "repos/tsanetgit/Connect-API-Code/contents/connect-core-api/src/main/resources/openapi.yaml?ref=beta" \
  -q .content | base64 --decode > third_party/connect-api/openapi.yaml
shasum -a 256 third_party/connect-api/openapi.yaml
gh api repos/tsanetgit/Connect-API-Code/commits/beta -q .sha
```

(`--decode` rather than `-d`: the short flag means something else in some
`base64` builds, and this is the one command here someone will paste blindly.)

Update the table above with the new commit, date and hash in the same commit as
the file. Treat a refresh as a reviewed change: regenerated client code can move
the connector's compile surface.

**This file and the pinned `connect-sdk-demo` ref in `ci.yml` are a matched
pair** — they are verified together by the sdk job. A bump PR moves both, or
states explicitly why the other did not need to move, and its passing sdk run is
the proof.

## Drift

Connector CI cannot detect drift — it has no access to the private upstream, by
design. The check belongs in `tsanet-ops`, which already snapshots this spec
hourly into `tsanet_ops.api_spec_snapshots` and holds the org token: compare the
latest snapshot's hash against the `sha256` recorded above. Drift is
**advisory** — pinning is what makes codegen deterministic, so a mismatch means
"refresh deliberately", not "the build is broken".
